title: Using AI for back testing
author: Worldly_Growth_50
selftext:
AI has become a hot topic in trading, especially back testing.

Some traders say it helps them test ideas faster, while others say it doesn't significantly improve the quality of results.

For those who are using AI for back testing, where has it been most effective? Finding new ideas, developing better strategies, or something else?

comments.author: Inevitable_Ad2727
comments.body:
Recently went through this myself with my own paper trading fleet. For me the value of AI isn't coming up with new ideas or making your trades better. Its use for me was getting faster at creating honest tests. I rewrote the exact strategy rules of my live bots into backtests overnight, something that would have taken me days by myself, and then tested the past five years of historical data across eleven different strategies.

Two things I learned doing it. First, AI will build you a flattering backtest if you let it. The valuable work was getting it to perform the unflattering tasks: accounting for real costs, assuming worst case scenario for fills (if a bar triggers both your stop loss and your profit target, assume you got stopped out), and forcing myself to write the rule down before testing it, so I wouldn't be able to adjust it based on the results.

Second, the results were ugly, and that was the point. My top performing live bot turned out to have the worst 5 year history of everything I tested. That tells me my live leaderboard is mostly noise right now, since a few weeks of live data is too small a sample to mean anything. Knowing that is worth more than some fancy looking backtest.

So where it's most effective, in my personal experience: turning "I need to test this" from a weekend long project into an afternoon, so you actually do it. Your own brain still has to run the process, especially the part where you accept results you don't like.

comments.author: tradematesHQ
comments.body:
AI backtesting is great at one thing: generating and killing ideas fast. You can test hundreds of variants and spot patterns you'd miss manually.

Where it fails is proving those ideas will work. Most "AI strategies" are overfit garbage. models that look genius on historical data because they memorized noise, not signal. The real danger is black-box execution: you don't know why it works, so you don't know when it stops.

That's why I use Trademates. They don't sell AI as a strategy generator; they publish the scoring model, backtest its outputs against forward returns, and show negative periods. Most vendors hide that. The data is not public free stock data bar enterprise API data which is only accessible with expensive paid subscription.

Use AI to find hypotheses. Validate them like a skeptic.
